title: Phase 17 — Infrastructure & Production Checkpoint
description: Optional checkpoint on serving, observability, and operational reliability.

questions.prompt: Dynamic batching on an inference server primarily trades off:
questions.explanation: Batching raises utilization/throughput, but requests wait for the batch window, adding queueing latency.

questions.prompt: A request trace is most useful for on-call diagnosis when it correlates a unique request ID across all stages of handling.
questions.explanation: Correlated trace IDs are what let one engineer follow a single failing request from ingress through model call to response.

questions.prompt: Which metric is typically the most direct autoscaling trigger for GPU inference?
options: Queue depth or time-to-first-token pressure with GPU utilization
questions.explanation: Queue depth / TTFT pressure reflects real demand vs capacity; utilization alone can mislead when batches are draining.

questions.prompt: Order a canary rollout with automated rollback:
options: Deploy new version to a small percentage of traffic
Watch SLO metrics (error rate, latency) on the canary
questions.explanation: Canary → observe → auto-rollback on breach → promote; skipping observation is how bad deploys become incidents.

questions.prompt: Select all honest ways to control LLM serving cost:
options: Caching repeated requests with semantic keys
Right-sizing model choice per task complexity
questions.explanation: Caching, task-appropriate models, and budgets control cost; inflating prompts raises cost and dilutes output quality.

questions.prompt: A rollback runbook is trustworthy when:
options: It exists as a notion page
It has been executed for real (or in a staged simulation) and lists exact commands plus verification steps
It assumes the previous version is still on every node
It redirects to the vendor console without verification
questions.explanation: Runbooks earn trust by being exercised with concrete steps and post-rollback verification; assumptions break at 3am.

questions.prompt: Define an SLO for your LLM service (pick one metric + threshold) and explain how an error budget changes your deployment decisions.

criteria: Links budget exhaustion to freezing rollouts / prioritizing reliability work

questions.explanation: Example: 'p95 end-to-end latency < 2s for 99% of requests over 30 days.' The 1% gap is your error budget: while it remains, feature deploys proceed; when it's spent, releases pause in favor of reliability work.
